observations: The corpus of record is new this round and the finding behind it is worth keeping. The implementer's October 23-spec list was lost with a drained pod and recorded nowhere; only the rule survived, 'the largest 23', and that rule does NOT seed - two attempts died after about nine minutes each on 82e744aa-3db7-4cdf-b840-e679b812de13.md, refused with `a table row holding 7 cells where its table has 5 ... a cell ends at every | not written \|, in code and links too, and at a | after an even run of backslashes`. A markdown rule I wrote to catch that let the same document through, because counting cells by splitting on unescaped pipes says 5 where the parser says 7. So the curator calls the reader instead of imitating it: pmdoc.Parse then Node.Validate over the bundle, 869 documents pass, the 23 largest are the corpus. The evidence that this reproduces the lost list rather than resembling it is the dump size: 11,374,504 bytes, which is what the implementer recorded in October from its own curation on another pod. Published as dispatch://INFRA-646/artifact/infra646-write-corpus-of-record-tgz with the list, the curator and the rule, and accepted by the implementer as the corpus of record for this issue.

My differential and the implementer's answer different questions and both are in the record. Mine is 6db39f4d against 751f4a5f - does THIS round's fold change a write - and both sides carry the same write_corpus_test.go, so nothing had to be copied between them. The implementer's is main dbdf9318 against 751f4a5f - does the whole change alter a write - and for that it had to copy the head's write_corpus_test.go onto the base tree, since the base carries an older copy without the seven extra edit kinds. It told me so unprompted. Neither reading subsumes the other and both are byte-equal.

The replay pairs and A5 are not re-run this round and carry from 1c9ce28b by the architect's ruling of 09:29Z, whose condition I verified at each head: the Go half of the branch's own diff against main is 1b8fd788ae228f9e2a0aa5f793ea63b12c7e827a0d91cff1bfb3f0a493361753 at e4118455, 1c9ce28b, 6db39f4d and c7c9fec0, and the only production change since is the fold above, which no non-nil path's behaviour depends on.
